test.name: Dispose completes a searched in_progress item and skips an unsearched planned one
test.description: The third test the step-mode plan names for this PR (Phase 1, prep PR 1): 'Dispose, named one `in_progress` item with a nil search entry and one `planned` item never searched, completes the first and skips the second (B).' Two rules meet here and they pull opposite ways, which is why one fixture must carry both. A search that RAN closes its item as `completed` even when it found nothing, and `research_append` REFUSES `skipped` there (planItemSearchedSkipInvariants, issue #3516, decision 9 of attached-records-baseline.md) -- a skip says nothing was searched, and research-exhaustiveness reads a disposed item as settled, so a skip after a search misstates the record. An item never searched is the opposite case and must NOT be completed, because completing it would claim a search nobody ran. Dispose previously acted on `planned` items only, so a searched `in_progress` item had no disposition at all and the declaration stayed refused forever.

input.delegation:
research-exhaustiveness refused the stop-gate declaration for q_001 because items on the active plan pl_002 are still open. Dispose of the named items: complete each whose search was done, or skip it with a skip_category.

questionId: q_001
planItemIds: pli_006, pli_004
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: GENERAL RULE UNDER TEST: how an item closes depends on whether its SEARCH RAN, not on the status it currently holds.
COMPLIANT: pli_006 ends at status 'completed', AND pli_004 ends at status 'skipped' with a skip_category.

pli_006 is `in_progress` and has a tied `record_search` log entry, so its search RAN. It must be `completed`. `research_append` refuses `skipped` on it, so completing it is not a stylistic preference but the only write the tool will accept. Marking it skipped, or leaving it `in_progress`, is the failure this test exists to catch: Dispose used to act on `planned` items only, so a searched `in_progress` item had no disposition and the declaration stayed refused.
pli_004 is `planned` with no tied log entry, so no search ran. It must be `skipped` with a skip_category, NOT completed -- completing it would claim a search nobody ran.
Do not require a particular skip_category for pli_004. The refusal reason is research-exhaustiveness's business; any category the agent can justify from the project is acceptable here.
pli_005 was not named in the delegation. Dispose acts on the ids it was given, so pli_005 changing status is a failure.
No new plan and no supersede: the stop criteria are already judged, and superseding would carry the same items into a new plan and re-block the gate.
The agent executes nothing itself and hands execution back to its caller, so do not grade whether any search ran.
